benchmark_metadata.name: BioIntel Empirical Evidence Benchmark (v1.0)
benchmark_metadata.description: Ground-truth evaluation benchmark of 20 verified experimental observations across four distinct biotechnology domains.

publication.title: Machine learning-aided engineering of hydrolases for PET depolymerization

observations.biological_model: Recombinant enzyme expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3)
observations.intervention: FAST-PETase (N233K/R224Q/S121E/D186H/R280A)
observations.assay: PET film depolymerization assay with HPLC quantification of terephthalic acid (TPA)
observations.endpoint: Depolymerization conversion percentage at 50 °C after 24 hours
observations.provenance_quote: FAST-PETase exhibited superior depolymerization capability, converting 52.3 ± 2.8% of post-consumer PET film to monomers at 50 °C within 24 h.
observations.limitations: Tested on amorphous PET film; crystallinity > 15% significantly reduces conversion rate.

publication.title: Machine learning-aided engineering of hydrolases for PET depolymerization

observations.intervention: FAST-PETase thermostability engineering
observations.statistical_test: Mean ± standard deviation across triplicate independent protein purifications
observations.provenance_quote: The apparent melting temperature of FAST-PETase was determined to be 67.8 ± 0.4 °C, representing a 19.0 °C increase over wild-type IsPETase (48.8 ± 0.3 °C).
observations.limitations: In vitro thermal shift in buffered aqueous solution; does not include organic co-solvents.

publication.title: An engineered PET depolymerase to break down and recycle plastic bottles

observations.intervention: LCC-ICCG variant (F243I/D238C/S283C/Y127G) at 3 mg/g PET loading
observations.control: Wild-type LCC and untreated micronized PET
observations.assay: HPLC quantification of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG)
observations.endpoint: PET depolymerization conversion percentage at 72 °C after 10 hours
observations.statistical_test: Mean of 3 independent reactor runs ± SD
observations.provenance_quote: The ICCG variant achieved 90% depolymerization of post-consumer PET into terephthalate in 10 h at 72 °C, with a productivity of 16.7 g/L/h of terephthalic acid.
observations.limitations: Requires pre-treatment extrusion and micronization to lower PET crystallinity below 10%.

publication.title: Structural basis of strigolactone perception by KAI2 in Pisum sativum

observations.intervention: Binding of (+)-5-deoxystrigol ((+)-5DS)
observations.provenance_quote: Addition of natural (+)-5DS induced a significant thermal shift of Delta Tm = +4.2 ± 0.3 °C in PsKAI2, whereas the non-natural enantiomer (-)-5DS caused no shift.
observations.limitations: Tested in isolated protein buffer; in planta perception requires D14/MAX2 signaling complex.

publication.title: Search-and-replace genome editing without double-strand breaks or donor DNA

observations.intervention: PE2 plasmid transfection targeting HEK3 locus
observations.statistical_test: Mean ± standard deviation of n=3 independent biological transfections
observations.provenance_quote: PE2 mediated targeted C->T conversion at the HEK3 site with 33.2 ± 2.1% efficiency, with 0.7 ± 0.1% indels.
observations.limitations: Transient plasmid transfection in immortalized transformed cells; efficiency varies widely across loci (5% to 50%).

publication.title: Search-and-replace genome editing without double-strand breaks or donor DNA

observations.intervention: PE3 (PE2 + non-target strand nicking sgRNA at +46 bp)
observations.control: PE2 alone without non-target strand nick
observations.statistical_test: Student t-test comparing PE3 to PE2 (p < 0.001)
observations.provenance_quote: Introduction of a second nick on the unedited strand (PE3) increased editing efficiency to 55.4 ± 3.4%, accompanied by a modest increase in indels to 1.7 ± 0.3%.
observations.limitations: Non-target strand nicking creates concurrent single-strand breaks that occasionally form double-strand breaks, elevating indel byproducts.

publication.title: Bi-PE: bi-directional prime editing for versatile and efficient genome manipulation

observations.intervention: Bi-PE dual pegRNA targeting RNF2
observations.provenance_quote: Bi-PE demonstrated a 52.4 ± 3.8% precise 3-bp insertion efficiency at the RNF2 site compared with 24.1 ± 2.6% for standard PE3.
observations.limitations: Requires simultaneous synthesis and delivery of two long pegRNAs (130-150 nt each).

publication.title: Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage

observations.intervention: BE3 plasmid targeting HEK site 2
observations.provenance_quote: Indel formation with BE3 remained below 0.1% (0.08 ± 0.02%) at all tested loci, whereas wild-type Cas9 induced 26% to 38% indels.
observations.limitations: Bystander cytosines within the 5-nt activity window (positions 4-8) are co-edited indiscriminately.

publication.title: Programmable base editing of A*T to G*C in genomic DNA without DNA cleavage

observations.intervention: ABE7.10 plasmid targeting 17 human genomic loci
observations.endpoint: Mean A->G conversion efficiency across target window
observations.provenance_quote: ABE7.10 mediated targeted A*T to G*C conversion with an average efficiency of approximately 50-53% across 17 target sites, with indel frequencies below 0.1%.
observations.limitations: Limited to transition mutations (A->G only); cannot perform transversions or insertions.

publication.title: Enhanced prime editing systems by manipulating cellular determinants of editing outcomes

observations.intervention: PEmax architecture (codon optimization + 34aa linker + engineered NLS)
observations.provenance_quote: PEmax yielded an average 2.8-fold increase in prime editing efficiency over PE2 across multiple genomic targets.
observations.limitations: In mismatch repair (MMR) proficient cells, MMR actively excises the 3-prime flap, reducing efficiency unless MLH1dn is co-expressed.

publication.title: A programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease in adaptive bacterial immunity

observations.intervention: SpCas9 programmed with single-guide RNA (sgRNA chimera A)
observations.assay: Agarose gel electrophoresis of plasmid digestion fragments
observations.provenance_quote: Chimeric sgRNA directed Cas9 to cleave target plasmid DNA with efficiency comparable to the dual crRNA:tracrRNA complex (>95% cleavage).
observations.limitations: In vitro naked DNA cleavage does not encounter chromatin condensation or histone barricades.

publication.title: Crystal structure of Cas9 in complex with guide RNA and target DNA

observations.intervention: X-ray diffraction analysis at 2.50 Angstrom resolution
observations.provenance_quote: The structure of Cas9 bound to sgRNA and target DNA was refined to Rwork = 0.198 and Rfree = 0.235 at 2.5 A resolution (PDB 4OO8).
observations.limitations: Static crystal lattice structure; does not capture continuous millisecond HNH domain conformational docking.

publication.title: Rewriting yeast central carbon metabolism for industrial isoprenoid production

observations.biological_model: Fed-batch fermentation in 200,000 L industrial bioreactor
observations.intervention: Isocitrate lyase/phosphoketolase synthetic pathway for acetyl-CoA generation
observations.assay: Gas chromatography with flame ionization detection (GC-FID)
observations.endpoint: Mass yield of farnesene on glucose (Y_p/s)
observations.statistical_test: Mean ± SD across 4 industrial manufacturing campaigns
observations.provenance_quote: The engineered strain achieved a farnesene yield on glucose of 0.245 g/g (73% of maximum theoretical yield) in commercial-scale production vessels.
observations.limitations: Requires strict micro-aerobic control and high-shear stirring; cooling demand is substantial during peak feeding.

publication.title: Rewriting yeast central carbon metabolism for industrial isoprenoid production

observations.intervention: Optimized fed-batch feeding profile
observations.provenance_quote: Final titers reached 130 ± 5 g/L farnesene after 120 h of fed-batch cultivation.
observations.limitations: Farnesene is an insoluble hydrocarbon phase; downstream requires continuous centrifugation and phase separation.

publication.title: High-level extracellular production of recombinant human lactoferrin in Pichia pastoris

observations.biological_model: Fed-batch stirred-tank bioreactor (5 L pilot scale)
observations.intervention: AOX1 promoter induction with co-expression of protein disulfide isomerase (PDI)
observations.endpoint: Secreted rhLF protein titer in clarified broth
observations.provenance_quote: Co-expression of PDI increased the extracellular titer of full-length folded rhLF to 4.8 ± 0.3 g/L following 96 h of methanol induction in a 5-L fermenter.
observations.limitations: Methanol feeding poses industrial flammability hazards; glycosylation pattern differs from native human breast milk lactoferrin (hypermannosylated).

publication.title: Production of the antimalarial drug precursor artemisinic acid in engineered yeast

observations.intervention: Co-expression of amorphadiene synthase (ADS) and cytochrome P450 CYP71AV1
observations.provenance_quote: Fed-batch fermentation of the optimized strain yielded artemisinic acid titers exceeding 25 g/L (25.0 ± 1.8 g/L).
observations.limitations: Requires semi-synthetic photochemical conversion from artemisinic acid to active artemisinin.

publication.title: Lipid nanoparticle delivery systems for mRNA vaccines and therapeutics

observations.intervention: Ionizable lipid ALC-0315 / SM-102 at 50:10:38.5:1.5 molar ratio
observations.statistical_test: Mean ± SD across 5 independent formulation batches
observations.provenance_quote: Ionizable lipid formulations consistently achieved high mRNA encapsulation efficiencies (>90%, averaging 94.5 ± 1.2%) with polydispersity indices < 0.1.
observations.limitations: Requires ultra-cold storage (-80 °C or -20 °C) to prevent hydrolysis of mRNA phosphodiester backbone.

publication.title: Efficacy and safety of the mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 vaccine

observations.intervention: mRNA-1273 (100 ug in SM-102 LNP, 2 doses at 28-day interval)
observations.statistical_test: Cox proportional hazards model (95% CI: 89.3% to 96.8%, p < 0.001)
observations.provenance_quote: Vaccine efficacy was 94.1% (95% CI, 89.3 to 96.8%; P<0.001) in preventing symptomatic illness starting 14 days after the second dose.
observations.limitations: Follow-up period of 64 days post-second dose; does not address multi-year durability or waning mucosal IgA titers.

publication.title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia

observations.biological_model: Phase 1/2 clinical trial in transfusion-dependent patients
observations.intervention: Ex vivo autologous CD34+ HSPCs edited at BCL11A erythroid enhancer via SpCas9 RNP electroporation
observations.assay: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) for fetal hemoglobin (HbF)
observations.endpoint: Fraction of total hemoglobin comprised of fetal hemoglobin (HbF)
observations.statistical_test: Longitudinal mean ± SD at 12 months post-infusion
observations.provenance_quote: At 12 months, the percentage of fetal hemoglobin rose to 43.1 ± 4.2% of total hemoglobin, eliminating vaso-occlusive episodes in all patients.
observations.limitations: Requires full myeloablative busulfan conditioning with associated risks of infertility, mucositis, and secondary cytopenias.

publication.title: Mechanisms of monoclonal antibody thermal aggregation and conformational stability

observations.biological_model: Formulated mAb solution (50 mg/mL in 20 mM histidine, pH 6.0)
observations.intervention: High-concentration thermal stress at 40 °C for 30 days
observations.statistical_test: Mean ± SD across triplicate stability chambers
observations.provenance_quote: SE-HPLC analysis confirmed 97.4 ± 0.2% monomer retention following 30 days of accelerated thermal stress at 40 °C, with soluble aggregate formation remaining below 1.5%.
observations.limitations: Accelerated stability test in liquid vial; does not simulate mechanical agitation or freeze-thaw cycles during cold-chain shipping.
